messages:
sarah: FYI Newton POC reporting slow TTFT on hosted sandbox — median ~1.2s, spikes to 2.8s. Customer expects <=300ms. Can we swarm?
ricardo: on it — can you paste request id + model + region + sample prompt? Also are they hitting any 429s?
sarah: request id rwd-prod-req-4821, model rwd-13b-ql8, region us-west-2, concurrency set to 8, batch window left default. sample prompt shortened: 'Summarize customer logs and suggest remediation.'
matt: quick callout: long prefill/prompt_prefix can push significant prefill work and delay first token. Also if prefill lands on a different shard we see KV cache cold misses. check for kv_cache_miss in logs.
olivia: I pulled logs around that request id — there are intermittent 429s then a bunch of slow responses. snippet: ```
[2026-03-22T14:03:12Z] rwd-prod-req-4821 INFO prefill_size=1424
[2026-03-22T14:03:12Z] rwd-prod-req-4821 WARN kv_cache_miss shard=3 key=0x7f3a
[2026-03-22T14:03:13Z] rwd-prod-req-4821 ERROR rate_limiter: throttle=1 code=429
[2026-03-22T14:03:14Z] rwd-prod-req-4821 INFO first_token_time_ms=1280
```
liz: a few suggestions we should try in the POC sandbox immediately: 1) enable prefill=true to warm KV cache on first request; 2) pin model variant to rwd-7b-ql8 for lower latency tests; 3) reduce batch window to 5ms for latency-sensitive route; 4) run a synthetic warmup of ~100 serialized small requests to populate caches.
sarah: customer also asking about pricing if we move them to reserved capacity to avoid throttling — can sales provide roughs?
ryan: for enterprise reserved capacity (small Dedicated pool) ballpark is ~18k/month per A100-equivalent for baseline commit; depends on commit length and region. We can run a sizing calc after we see stable QPS and token rates.
raj: security question from their infosec: they require KMS/HSM, SOC2 audit report, and retained audit logs for 1 year. We can offer Private (VPC) + KMS integration. I'll drop the questionnaire link.
raj: https://redwood-internal/legal/sec-questionnaire/newton (shared doc)
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment started -> canary-id=canary-2026-03-22-14-25; target us-west-2; config: prefill=true, batch_window_ms=5, pin_model=rwd-7b-ql8
matt: great. after the canary finishes, please re-run the customer sample 20x and capture first_token_time_ms distribution and kv_cache_miss counts. If TTFT drops under 300ms median we can recommend switching route policy for their traffic.
olivia: FYI I also see a small spike in concurrent connections from their integration that lines up with the 429s — they were ramping concurrency from 4 -> 16 over 30s which likely tripped rate limits.
sarah: ok action items for the POC: enable prefill, pin smaller variant for latency tests, run 100 warmup requests serialized, collect logs (first_token_time_ms + kv_cache_miss + rate_limiter events), provide sizing for reserved capacity, share security questionnaire. I've scheduled a call with Newton on 2026-03-25 10:00 PT to review results. tagging folks: @ricardo @matt @liz @ryan @raj :rocket:
ricardo: I'll take logs and follow up with a short runbook steps we can hand the customer. Expect a message in this thread when I have the numbers.
liz: I'll draft the short customer-facing checklist (prefill toggle, batch window change, warmup script).
ryan: prepping rough reserved-capacity deck for the call.
raj: I'll follow up on KMS and data residency clarifications during the call.
sarah: thanks team. Newton rep will join with their engineer on Thu. I'll drop the runbook + results before the call. :thumbsup:
